title: Ahaan Panday Is Shooting His First Dance Number in Manchester — and It's a Bigger Deal Than You Think
excerpt: The 'Saiyaara' star is filming an energetic sequence in Ali Abbas Zafar's upcoming film, marking a new phase for Bollywood's next-gen action hero and the UK's growing role in Hindi cinema.
body:
Somewhere in Manchester right now, a Bollywood dance sequence is being choreographed. And the person at the centre of it is a 20-something who first went viral not for a film — but for absolutely tearing up the dance floor at his sister’s wedding.

Ahaan Panday, the young actor who made his Bollywood debut with Mohit Suri’s musical romance *Saiyaara*, is in the UK for a four-day shoot that marks his first-ever on-screen dance number. The sequence is part of Ali Abbas Zafar’s upcoming film, backed by Yash Raj Films, and it signals a deliberate expansion of Panday’s screen presence from dramatic actor to full-spectrum Bollywood leading man.

## The Wedding Video That Started Everything

Before *Saiyaara*, before YRF, before Ali Abbas Zafar — there was a wedding video.

When Ahaan’s sister Alanna Panday got married, footage of him dancing at the reception went massively viral. The energy was infectious, the moves were surprisingly polished, and the internet collectively decided: this guy belongs on screen.

That viral moment, combined with his family connections — he’s part of the extended Panday clan that includes cousin Ananya Panday and uncle Chunky Panday — created the kind of buzz that Bollywood’s star-making machinery loves to work with. But unlike many nepo-baby debuts that fizzle after the first film, Ahaan has been methodically building his credentials.

## Building the Action Hero

The Manchester shoot isn’t just about dance. Ahaan’s role in Zafar’s film is an action-heavy character that has required months of preparation. He’s been training in boxing, martial arts, and strength conditioning to portray what’s being described as a “fierce, action-ready” character — a sharp pivot from the romantic softness of *Saiyaara*.

Ali Abbas Zafar, the director behind *Sultan*, *Tiger Zinda Hai*, and *Bharat*, is known for mounting large-scale action spectacles. The fact that he’s chosen Ahaan for this kind of role — and that YRF is bankrolling it — suggests the industry is betting on Panday as a long-term action star, not just a one-film wonder.

Sharvari Wagh, fresh off her breakout year, has been confirmed as the female lead opposite Ahaan. The pairing of two young, commercially viable stars under Zafar’s direction and YRF’s production banner makes this one of the most closely watched next-gen Bollywood projects in development.

## Why Manchester?

Bollywood’s love affair with the UK is nothing new — *Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge* turned the Swiss-British tourism corridor into a pilgrimage route. But for decades, “UK” in Bollywood meant London. Maybe Scotland for the odd song sequence.

Manchester is a different choice, and it’s a telling one. The city has one of the largest South Asian communities in England, a thriving Desi food and culture scene, and — crucially — the kind of film-friendly infrastructure and tax incentives that are pulling international productions away from London.

For the hundreds of thousands of NRIs living in Manchester, Leeds, Birmingham, and across the North of England, seeing their city in a major Bollywood film isn’t just a novelty — it’s recognition. When Bollywood shoots in your neighbourhood, it tells a story about where the diaspora actually lives, not just where tourism boards want them to visit.

## What’s Next

The four-day dance shoot in Manchester is one piece of a larger production schedule that’s still being finalised. With Zafar’s track record of delivering commercially massive films and YRF’s marketing machinery behind it, the project is positioned as one of 2026-27’s most anticipated releases.

For Ahaan Panday, the stakes are clear: this is the film that decides whether his debut was a beginning or a peak. The wedding video got him noticed. *Saiyaara* got him in the door. Manchester is where he shows he can stay.
